text.p: Macquarie Bank Ltd said on Monday it was optimistic about its performance for the six months to March 31, 1997, following trading in October and November.

"Although it is too early to make a forecast, we are optimistic about the second half," chairman David Clarke told reporters. "It may be difficult to match the result of the second half of last year, which was a very strong result, but we are confident we can least match that result or even better it and there has been nothing to change that view following the trading for the first two months of this half," Clarke said.

Macquarie Bank, which is 13.4 percent owned by the Brunei Investment Agency (BIA), earlier reported a 21.3 percent rise in first half net profit to A$46.03 million in the six months to September 30, 1996.
Macquarie said all divisions contributed to the profit rise.
Managing director Allan Moss said he was confident the bank's underwriting business would continue to perform strongly in the second half.
Moss said the bank was currently very active right across all its operations. "We are busy right across the board. There is a lot of activity in all our operations," he said.
Moss said the near 400 percent increase in profit from its stockbroking arm Macquarie Equities Ltd was due partly to an increase in market share, but mainly due to market volume.
At 12.20 p.m. (0120 GMT), Macquarie shares were six cents down at A$8.60.
